summary: Instagram Reels is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets 100 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 50 views. The best performers are relatable sensor topics with a question or surprising hook, and they earn shares and saves, which is a strong sign. Many videos are near-duplicate topics (smoke alarm, IR sensor, tap) that split attention and score low, and the one English video only worked on YouTube.
winningPattern: Hindi Reels about a sensor or gadget people meet in daily life or in robotics projects (PIR motion sensor, robot IR obstacle sensor, clap switch, street light). The title opens with a surprising claim or a 'Kaise' question, such as 'Aapko Dekhta Nahi!' or 'Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', followed by one emoji. Posted mainly on Instagram, where shares and saves come from a clear 'myth vs reality' reveal and a maker-friendly project angle.
doMore: Open with a contradiction or myth-buster hook ('X nahi, Y se kaam karta hai') as the clap switch and PIR videos do
Pick maker-relevant topics tied to a buildable project (robot, clap switch, PIR alarm) and end with 'save this for your project'
Add a clear share or save prompt, since the top videos draw the most shares and saves
Publish one topic per concept and make each one distinct instead of remaking the same sensor
Test YouTube separately: try a stronger first-second visual and a shorter title, or concentrate on Reels until YouTube picks up
stopDoing: Repeating near-identical topics (three smoke/IR/tap variants) with only the title changed
Generic 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' titles with no surprising claim, like the phone orientation, mall door and touchscreen videos
Mixing in English videos without a plan, since the Arduino Uno video got zero Instagram reach
